sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你 20 多岁的心理学》，在这个播客里，我们探讨 20 多岁时会经历的一些重大生活变化和过渡，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本期播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of your 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老朋友，无论你身处世界何地，很高兴你能回来收听新一期节目，当然，我们将继续剖析你 20 多岁的心理。

sentences.en: Today, we are going to be talking about a pretty significant emotion, a very core emotion and experience, both in our 20s and I think beyond, and that is the experience of panic,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讨论一种非常重要的情绪，一种在我们 20 多岁甚至以后都非常核心的情绪和体验，那就是恐慌的体验，

sentences.en: of fear, intense alarm, terror, whatever you want to call it, but specifically, we are going to be addressing panic attacks, that sudden onset of extreme dread and anxiety
sentences.zh: 恐惧、强烈的警觉、惊恐，无论你怎么称呼它，但具体来说，我们要讨论的是恐慌发作，那种极度恐惧和焦虑的突然来袭，

sentences.en: that engulfs us, normally in response to some threat in the environment, whether that is real or perceived.
sentences.zh: 它会吞噬我们，通常是对环境中某种威胁的反应，无论这种威胁是真实的还是感知的。

sentences.en: Panic attacks are a terrible sensation, really, and I'm saying that as, of course, someone who has had for years experience these as kind of part of my daily, weekly, monthly life,
sentences.zh: 说实话，恐慌发作是一种可怕的感觉，我这么说是因为，作为一个多年来一直将其作为日常生活、每周、每月一部分的人，我深有体会，

sentences.en: often in response to things that I couldn't even identify or which were so ambiguous and non-worrisome in hindsight that I felt like I didn't even know
sentences.zh: 这些发作通常是对一些我甚至无法识别的事情做出的反应，或者事后看来，这些事情是如此模糊且不值得担心，以至于我甚至不知道

sentences.en: why these panic attacks were occurring in the first place.
sentences.zh: 为什么这些恐慌发作会发生。

sentences.en: They were just coming out of the blue, really, and that sense of confusion, and more specifically, I think a lack of control felt equally scary.
sentences.zh: 它们真的就是毫无征兆地出现了，那种困惑感，更具体地说，我觉得那种失控感同样令人恐惧。

sentences.en: And I think this idea or the sensation that I couldn't control what my mind or my body was choosing to do kind of kept that cycle continuing because I began to fear the sensation
sentences.zh: 我认为这种无法控制大脑或身体行为的感觉，反而让这种循环持续下去，因为我开始害怕这种感觉，

sentences.en: and fear the fear of a panic attack rather than anything in particular.
sentences.zh: 害怕恐慌发作带来的恐惧，而不是害怕任何具体的事情。

sentences.en: And the more I think I began to actually learn about why that was, how that happened, what a panic attack is, the more I really felt that sense of control I needed,
sentences.zh: 我想，当我开始真正了解为什么会这样、它是如何发生的、什么是恐慌发作时，我越发感受到了我所需要的控制感，

sentences.en: not just a control over the bodily sensations that accompany this experience, the racing heartbeat, the shortness of breath, the tingles, the mental spiral,
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是对伴随这种体验的身体感觉的控制，比如心跳加速、呼吸急促、刺痛感、思维混乱，

sentences.en: but I also just increased this feeling of capability.
sentences.zh: 我还增强了这种掌控感。

sentences.en: I felt like I had a newfound ability to cope and to see panic as no more than just an emotion, an evolutionary response to my environment,
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己获得了一种新的应对能力，能够将恐慌仅仅视为一种情绪，一种对环境的进化反应，

sentences.en: an alarm system that was unfortunately broken for me.
sentences.zh: 一个对我来说不幸坏掉了的警报系统。

sentences.en: And although it was quite debilitating for a while, I used to get these like really intense week or month-long periods where I was having them twice a day consistently,
sentences.zh: 虽然它曾一度让我非常痛苦，我曾经有过一段非常强烈的时期，持续一周或一个月，每天都会发作两次，

sentences.en: I do now feel like I'm at this point where I understand why that happened and I learnt from it and I learnt the best ways I think of dealing with this very weird sensation,
sentences.zh: 但我现在觉得我已经到了这样一个阶段：我理解了为什么会发生这种情况，我从中吸取了教训，并且我认为我已经学会了处理这种非常奇怪的感觉、

sentences.en: with this very unique type of fear.
sentences.zh: 这种非常独特的恐惧的最佳方法。

sentences.en: And we're going to talk about it today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们就来聊聊这个话题。

sentences.en: I want to talk you through my best tips for coping, tell you about what I've learned and kind of provide you with the ultimate guide to panic attacks.
sentences.zh: 我想和你分享我应对恐慌的最佳建议，告诉你我学到了什么，并为你提供一份关于恐慌发作的终极指南。

sentences.en: We're going to discuss the true causes, some of the misconceptions, the distinction between panic and anxiety and why it is that some people, perhaps like you and I,
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论其真正原因、一些误区、恐慌与焦虑的区别，以及为什么有些人，也许就像你和我一样，

sentences.en: have this weird, misguided,
sentences.zh: 拥有这种奇怪的、被误导的、

sentences.en: malfunctioning alarm system.
sentences.zh: 功能失调的警报系统。

sentences.en: I always think that psychoeducation, talking about the problem, is such a valuable tool to begin with when it comes to anything really
sentences.zh: 我一直认为，心理教育，即谈论问题本身，是处理任何事情时非常有价值的起点，

sentences.en: because how can we feel in control of our panic if we don't even know where it's coming from, if we don't even understand its emotional, biological, psychological origin,
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们连恐慌的来源都不知道，如果我们不理解它的情感、生物学和心理学起源，我们怎么能感到自己掌控了恐慌呢？

sentences.en: when we understand that psychology.
sentences.zh: 当我们理解了其中的心理学原理，

sentences.en: We no longer feel like panic attacks are some big, scary visitor that we can't get rid of.
sentences.zh: 我们就不会再觉得恐慌发作是一个我们无法摆脱的巨大、可怕的访客。

sentences.en: They're just something a lot more simple and tame.
sentences.zh: 它们只是变得简单且温和多了。

sentences.en: They are a series of bodily and mental reactions that have just gotten their wires crossed.
sentences.zh: 它们只是一系列身体和心理反应，只是线路接错了而已。

sentences.en: It's this combination of sensations that is meant to be helpful, but right now it's not.
sentences.zh: 这是一种本意是为了提供帮助，但现在却适得其反的感觉组合。

sentences.en: And that is all that it is.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: It is not some big physical thing that is going to come in and ruin your life.
sentences.zh: 它不是什么会突然出现并毁掉你生活的重大生理疾病。

sentences.en: You are not going to pass away.
sentences.zh: 你不会因此而离世。

sentences.en: You are not going to die.
sentences.zh: 你不会死。

sentences.en: You are not going to feel like this forever.
sentences.zh: 你不会永远有这种感觉。

sentences.en: You will exhaust yourself.
sentences.zh: 你只会感到精疲力竭。

sentences.en: You will get through this.
sentences.zh: 你会挺过去的。

sentences.en: So let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们来谈谈它。

sentences.en: Before we start, a little PSA that the final five, six minutes of this episode are a short relaxation audio if you are having a panic attack right now.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前，先做一个小提醒：本期节目的最后五六分钟是一段简短的放松音频，如果你现在正在经历恐慌发作，可以听一听。

sentences.en: So if you want to listen to that, please see the timestamp in the description.
sentences.zh: 如果你想听的话，请查看描述中的时间戳。

sentences.en: And if you are returning to this episode, here is your reminder to feel free to skip ahead if that is what you're here for.
sentences.zh: 如果你是回头来听这期节目的，这里提醒你，如果你是为了那个音频而来，可以随意跳过前面的内容。

sentences.en: But let's get started.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Learning to deal with overwhelming and intense emotions is kind of part of our journey as humans for some more than others.
sentences.zh: 学习如何处理压倒性的强烈情绪，是我们作为人类旅程的一部分，对某些人来说更是如此。

sentences.en: But I also don't think that the end goal, when we're talking about panic attacks or any emotion that is scary, I don't think that the end goal
sentences.zh: 但我也不认为，当我们谈论恐慌发作或任何可怕的情绪时，最终目标

sentences.en: should be complete emotional regulation to never feel any negative emotions, constant peace and tranquility.
sentences.zh: 应该是完全的情绪调节，即永远不感受任何负面情绪，保持恒久的平静与安宁。

sentences.en: Because I think that's depriving ourselves of some of the useful things that any emotion does for us, some of the useful things that panic does for us.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为那是在剥夺我们从任何情绪中获得的有益之处，剥夺恐慌能为我们带来的一些有益之处。

sentences.en: I know that that sounds a little bit ridiculous, as uncomfortable as panic attacks are.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来有点荒谬，毕竟恐慌发作是非常不舒服的。

sentences.en: I actually think that the worst thing we can do for ourselves, either before, during or after, is try and ignore it, to avoid or suppress the sensations of anxiety
sentences.zh: 但我实际上认为，我们在发作前、发作中或发作后能做的最糟糕的事情，就是试图忽视它，通过匆忙行事、分散注意力或将其推开来避免或压抑焦虑和恐惧的感觉，

sentences.en: and fear by rushing through, by distracting, by pushing them aside, because eventually it will make them stronger.
sentences.zh: 因为最终这只会让它们变得更强烈。

sentences.en: I think that seems really counterintuitive, especially if you're someone who has a panic disorder and you experience these very regularly.
sentences.zh: 我认为这看起来非常反直觉，特别是如果你患有恐慌症并且经常经历这些发作的话。

sentences.en: It is natural to have a lot of fear towards the incidence and the prevalence of your panic attacks, right?
sentences.zh: 对恐慌发作的发生频率和普遍性感到恐惧是很自然的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, no one wants to be in a place where they're feeling this uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，没有人愿意处在那种让自己如此不舒服的状态中。

sentences.en: And so, naturally, we want to push them away.
sentences.zh: 所以，自然而然地，我们想要推开它们。

sentences.en: We want to run away.
sentences.zh: 我们想要逃跑。

sentences.en: We want to put our panic, our panic attacks, our anxiety in this box and hide it and hope to never hear from it again.
sentences.zh: 我们想要把恐慌、恐慌发作、焦虑关进盒子里，藏起来，希望永远不要再听到它们的声音。

sentences.en: When we rely too heavily, though, on avoidance, especially when it comes to feelings of panic, this only causes us to focus on them more intensely.
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们过度依赖回避时，特别是在面对恐慌感时，这只会让我们更强烈地关注它们。

sentences.en: It also gives them more power because the act of fearing fear, which is essentially what you're doing by avoiding something, increases that fear.
sentences.zh: 这也赋予了它们更多的力量，因为“恐惧恐惧”的行为——这本质上就是你在回避某事时所做的——会增加那种恐惧。

sentences.en: Now, I know that sounds very convoluted, but when we refuse to experience intense emotions like panic, we don't actually learn the skills to deal with them in the long run
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很复杂，但当我们拒绝体验像恐慌这样强烈的情绪时，我们实际上并没有学会在长期内处理它们的技能，

sentences.en: because we never have any practice.
sentences.zh: 因为我们从来没有练习过。

sentences.en: It also just causes them to return,
sentences.zh: 这也只会导致它们卷土重来，

sentences.en: I would say the best word is to return stronger because every time we avoid thinking or feeling about our anxiety, it in many ways kind of returns with a vengeance
sentences.zh: 我想最好的词是“变本加厉地卷土重来”，因为每次我们回避思考或感受焦虑时，它在许多方面都会以更猛烈的姿态回归，

sentences.en: because we never provide it with an outlet.
sentences.zh: 因为我们从未给它提供一个宣泄的出口。

sentences.en: And secondly, we never allow ourselves to truly acknowledge what might be triggering our fear, whether it's internal or external, because we are so scared of looking
sentences.zh: 其次，我们从未允许自己真正承认是什么在触发我们的恐惧，无论是内部还是外部的，因为我们太害怕直视

sentences.en: at our fear directly.
sentences.zh: 我们的恐惧了。

sentences.en: We are so scared of examining it.
sentences.zh: 我们太害怕去审视它了。

sentences.en: Now, what is it that triggers a panic attack?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底是什么触发了恐慌发作呢？

sentences.en: Panic is what we call a survival emotion.
sentences.zh: 恐慌是我们所说的“生存情绪”。

sentences.en: It is a reaction that serves the function of preparing us to fight off or escape danger by creating and triggering a fear that is so strong
sentences.zh: 这是一种旨在帮助我们通过制造和触发强烈的恐惧来准备战斗或逃离危险的功能性反应，

sentences.en: that it prevents all rational and logical thinking.
sentences.zh: 这种恐惧如此强烈，以至于它阻止了所有理性和逻辑思考。

sentences.en: And it causes us to only really focus on that one thing in our environment or in our mind that we see as dangerous or threatening.
sentences.zh: 它使我们只关注环境中或脑海中我们认为危险或具有威胁性的那一件事情。

sentences.en: So in this way, panic is the result of our fight or flight response.
sentences.zh: 因此，恐慌是我们的“战斗或逃跑”反应的结果。

sentences.en: This response is very evolutionary.
sentences.zh: 这种反应是非常进化的产物。

sentences.en: It also now includes freeze and it's essentially the automatic urge we have to address danger and ensure our survival by either fighting back against this force,
sentences.zh: 它现在还包括“僵住”反应，本质上是我们应对危险并确保生存的自动冲动，通过反击这种力量、

sentences.en: whatever it may be, running away, or in some cases becoming paralyzed and being unable to really do anything.
sentences.zh: 无论它是什么，逃跑，或者在某些情况下变得瘫痪，无法真正做任何事情。

sentences.en: This is triggered by something that we see as dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这是由我们认为危险的事物触发的。

sentences.en: I think most people know this, obviously.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人都知道这一点，显然。

sentences.en: This automatic response is for our survival.
sentences.zh: 这种自动反应是为了我们的生存。

sentences.en: It came, it has developed for many, many, many generations.
sentences.zh: 它经过了许多、许多、许多代的进化和发展。

sentences.en: And in the past, the purpose that it served for our ancestors was that if there was a very real physical threat, like a big hungry lion or an oncoming flood
sentences.zh: 在过去，它为我们的祖先服务的功能是，如果存在非常真实的物理威胁，比如一只饥饿的大狮子或即将来临的洪水，

sentences.en: or a sinister neighbouring tribe approaching us with weapons, we needed this panic to basically indicate to us to get away or to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 或者一个带着武器向我们逼近的邪恶邻近部落，我们需要这种恐慌来基本指示我们逃跑或采取行动。

sentences.en: Those were the threats that we faced when this automatic function and process first evolved and came about.
sentences.zh: 这就是这种自动功能和过程最初进化和出现时我们所面临的威胁。

sentences.en: Nowadays, these same triggers are still kind of present, maybe not a lion.
sentences.zh: 如今，同样的触发因素依然存在，也许不是狮子。

sentences.en: I don't know where you're living though, but more commonly, these triggers can be anything that we perceive as dangerous, sudden, stressful or acute events,
sentences.zh: 虽然我不知道你住在哪里，但更常见的是，这些触发因素可以是任何我们认为危险、突然、压力大或急性的事件，

sentences.en: but also a number of internal triggers, phobias, really bad, dark thoughts, certain stimulants like caffeine, ongoing stress, many other things.
sentences.zh: 但也包括许多内部触发因素，如恐惧症、非常糟糕的阴暗想法、某些兴奋剂（如咖啡因）、持续的压力等等。

sentences.en: Anything that evokes fear will as a result activate our fight or flight response because the part of us that is activating that response is not very intelligent.
sentences.zh: 任何引发恐惧的事物都会激活我们的“战斗或逃跑”反应，因为激活该反应的那部分大脑并不太聪明。

sentences.en: It is not rational.
sentences.zh: 它不理性。

sentences.en: It is not, does not really have critical thinking skills.
sentences.zh: 它没有批判性思维能力。

sentences.en: It is just meant to be there almost like an instantaneous alarm system.
sentences.zh: 它只是像一个即时警报系统一样存在。

sentences.en: It is meant to be responding rapidly and when something responds rapidly,
sentences.zh: 它旨在快速反应，而当某物快速反应时，

sentences.en: as in this system, it doesn't have the time to really process what this thing that's scaring us really means, whether it actually is truly dangerous.
sentences.zh: 就像这个系统一样，它没有时间真正处理让我们害怕的东西到底意味着什么，它是否真的危险。

sentences.en: So when this automatic response is activated, a particular part of our nervous system known as our sympathetic nervous system goes to work switching on all the bodily functions
sentences.zh: 因此，当这种自动反应被激活时，我们神经系统中被称为“交感神经系统”的特定部分就会开始工作，开启所有我们

sentences.en: that we will need the most for immediate survival and switching off all of those that we don't need.
sentences.zh: 即时生存最需要的身体功能，并关闭所有我们不需要的功能。

sentences.en: So things like our digestive system, our sexual organs as a way to divert energy away from one thing, from one part of our body and put all of that energy to the systems
sentences.zh: 比如消化系统、性器官，这是一种将能量从身体的一个部位转移到另一个部位的方式，并将所有能量投入到那些

sentences.en: that are going to help us with the threat in front of us.
sentences.zh: 将帮助我们应对眼前威胁的系统中。

sentences.en: It floods us with norepinephrine, with adrenaline, cortisol to get the body ready to fight, flee or freeze and this subsequently triggers the symptoms that we associate
sentences.zh: 它会用去甲肾上腺素、肾上腺素、皮质醇充斥我们的身体，让身体准备好战斗、逃跑或僵住，这随后触发了我们与

sentences.en: with a panic attack.
sentences.zh: 恐慌发作相关的症状。

sentences.en: All of those bodily reactions, a racing heart, sweating, dizziness, trembling, hot flushes, maybe that tingling in your arm, that tightness in your chest,
sentences.zh: 所有这些身体反应，心跳加速、出汗、头晕、颤抖、潮热，也许还有手臂的刺痛感、胸部的紧绷感，

sentences.en: a sense of imminent danger, spiraling thoughts.
sentences.zh: 一种迫在眉睫的危险感，思维混乱。

sentences.en: These sensations are caused by our body, they're caused by our involuntary response to danger.
sentences.zh: 这些感觉是由我们的身体引起的，是由我们对危险的非自愿反应引起的。

sentences.en: For example, that tingling sensation we were just talking about, that's actually caused by blood vessels constricting and increasing blood to the heart so that we can run faster,
sentences.zh: 例如，我们刚才谈到的那种刺痛感，实际上是由血管收缩和增加流向心脏的血液引起的，这样我们才能跑得更快、

sentences.en: fight harder but it also leaves less blood flow to the rest of the body causing that strange feeling in our limbs.
sentences.zh: 打得更猛，但这也会导致流向身体其他部位的血液减少，从而引起四肢那种奇怪的感觉。

sentences.en: Those hot flushes that we often experience, that's just caused by an increase in body temperature because of the effect of those crucial stress hormones.
sentences.zh: 我们经常经历的那些潮热，只是因为那些关键的压力荷尔蒙的影响导致体温升高。

sentences.en: All of those sensations that we fear, that we associate with a panic attack, are nothing more than our body doing what it evolved to do best, which is to help us survive.
sentences.zh: 所有我们害怕的、与恐慌发作相关的感觉，只不过是我们的身体在做它进化出最擅长的事情，即帮助我们生存。

sentences.en: But sometimes we actually misinterpret those sensations and we begin to think it means something more, it means something in our body has gone wrong and that just causes our panic
sentences.zh: 但有时我们实际上误解了这些感觉，开始认为这意味着更多，意味着我们身体出了问题，这只会导致我们的恐慌

sentences.en: and our fear to accelerate.
sentences.zh: 和恐惧加速。

sentences.en: The biggest one for me is when my heart starts racing and I think for sure
sentences.zh: 对我来说最严重的是当我的心跳开始加速时，我肯定会认为

sentences.en: I'm going to have a heart attack,
sentences.zh: 我要心脏病发作了，

sentences.en: I'm going to die,
sentences.zh: 我要死了，

sentences.en: I can't slow my heart rate down, this big essential life-giving organ is going to burst in my chest and what I know now is that that is the beginning of fearing the fear
sentences.zh: 我无法让心率慢下来，这个重要的生命器官要在我的胸腔里爆裂了，而我现在知道的是，这就是“恐惧恐惧”的开始，

sentences.en: because I'm fearing the sensations,
sentences.zh: 因为我在害怕这些感觉，

sentences.en: I'm not actually fearing the thing that caused those sensations in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我并不是在害怕最初导致这些感觉的事情本身。

sentences.en: We get more worried about that than the actual danger, about our perception of danger.
sentences.zh: 我们对这些感觉的担心比对实际危险的担心还要多，比对危险的感知还要多。

sentences.en: If you are someone who has a panic disorder, meaning you experience more frequent panic attacks of an increased severity, you also begin to fear having an attack at the wrong time,
sentences.zh: 如果你患有恐慌症，意味着你更频繁地经历严重程度增加的恐慌发作，你也会开始害怕在错误的时间发作，

sentences.en: maybe during a lecture, at work, during a date and this begins to become quite debilitating because you kind of have to fight back against that very instinctual, natural,
sentences.zh: 比如在讲座期间、在工作中、在约会时，这开始变得非常令人痛苦，因为你必须对抗那种非常本能的、自然的、

sentences.en: normal urge to avoid those situations where you're going to feel exposed.
sentences.zh: 正常的、想要回避那些会让你感到暴露的场合的冲动。

sentences.en: You don't want to be in a public place or in front of other people and having this sense of fear and that can actually lead to anticipatory anxiety and that is that kind of
sentences.zh: 你不想在公共场合或在别人面前感到这种恐惧，这实际上会导致预期性焦虑，这就是那种

sentences.en: constant panic that you will have a panic attack, that you will experience a panic attack when it's inconvenient, when you are unprepared and the thing about panic attacks,
sentences.zh: 持续担心自己会恐慌发作的心理，担心在不方便的时候、在毫无准备的时候经历恐慌发作，而关于恐慌发作的事情，

sentences.en: specifically those caused by a panic disorder or even a phobia, is that they are often directed towards things that don't pose an immediate threat, that are not going to kill us
sentences.zh: 特别是那些由恐慌症甚至恐惧症引起的恐慌发作，是它们通常针对那些并不构成直接威胁、不会杀死我们的事物，

sentences.en: but that natural and instinctive alarm system has become broken so that it starts firing off warning signs and getting the body prepared for survival in response to a whole
sentences.zh: 但那个自然且本能的警报系统已经坏掉了，以至于它开始发出警告信号，并让身体准备好生存，以应对各种

sentences.en: array of triggers.
sentences.zh: 触发因素。

sentences.en: Everybody has an internal alarm system that warns them of when they are in danger.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有一个内部警报系统，在他们处于危险时发出警告。

sentences.en: You need that.
sentences.zh: 你需要它。

sentences.en: It's important.
sentences.zh: 它很重要。

sentences.en: But with anxiety or a panic disorder, our alarm system has kind of become a bit miscalibrated, a bit faulty, way too sensitive, meaning that our threshold for what we should panic
sentences.zh: 但对于焦虑症或恐慌症患者来说，我们的警报系统已经变得有点校准失准，有点故障，过于敏感，这意味着我们对应该恐慌的

sentences.en: about is much lower than other people's.
sentences.zh: 阈值比其他人低得多。

sentences.en: the analogy I think we talk about a lot is having a faulty car alarm, for example.
sentences.zh: 我们经常谈论的一个类比是汽车警报器故障，例如。

sentences.en: You know, the normal car alarm should really only go off when someone is like out the side of your window with a baseball bat trying to steal your CDs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正常的汽车警报器应该只在有人拿着棒球棍在窗外试图偷你的 CD 时才会响。

sentences.en: Like, it should be triggered by things that are actually going to like cause the car to break down or be broken into.
sentences.zh: 它应该被那些真正会导致汽车损坏或被闯入的事情触发。

sentences.en: But in the brain of someone with anxiety or a panic disorder, that alarm is a lot more sensitive.
sentences.zh: 但在焦虑症或恐慌症患者的大脑中，那个警报器要敏感得多。

sentences.en: So using that car analogy, it could be triggered by a leaf falling on the roof.
sentences.zh: 所以用那个汽车类比来说，它可能只是因为一片树叶掉在车顶上就被触发了。

sentences.en: And that is enough to set everything off, to get everything going.
sentences.zh: 而这足以引发一切，让一切开始运转。

sentences.en: I think knowing that that is what causes some people to panic more than others was really comforting to me.
sentences.zh: 我认为知道这就是导致有些人比其他人更容易恐慌的原因，对我来说真的很安慰。

sentences.en: And there are a number of reasons that might cause this lowered threshold for emotional and physiological arousal.
sentences.zh: 导致这种情绪和生理唤醒阈值降低的原因有很多。

sentences.en: These include things like a family history of panic attacks.
sentences.zh: 其中包括恐慌症家族史等因素。

sentences.en: We know that genetics and DNA play such a huge role in a lot of mental health conditions, but also a past traumatic event that has caused you to become hyper vigilant to your
sentences.zh: 我们知道遗传和DNA在许多心理健康状况中起着巨大的作用，但过去的创伤性事件也会让你对周围环境和自身内部状态变得过度警觉，这几乎是一种为了避免该事件再次发生、避免未来创伤的生存技能。

sentences.en: surroundings and to your own internal state as almost a survival skill to avoid that event happening again, to avoid future trauma.
sentences.zh: 周围环境以及你自身内在的状态，这几乎是一种为了避免此类事件再次发生、为了避免未来创伤而习得的生存技能。

sentences.en: Another example is really major life changes or shifts that are taking so much energy from you already, that there are very few mental resources left over to cope
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是重大的生活变动或转变，它们已经消耗了你太多的精力，以至于几乎没有剩余的心理资源来应对

sentences.en: with small things.
sentences.zh: 小事了。

sentences.en: That's why we often see someone who has maybe gone through like a big breakup, they've left their job, they've moved, and then suddenly they're having a panic
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们经常看到有人可能刚经历了一场重大的分手、离职或搬家，然后突然因为一些在别人看来非常非常微不足道的事情而恐慌，比如找不到车钥匙，或者别人随口说的一句小话，

sentences.en: attack about something that everyone else would think is super super minor, like not being able to find their car keys or some small comment that someone has said to them
sentences.zh: 因为一些在别人看来极其微不足道的事情而发作，比如找不到车钥匙，或者别人随口说的一句小评论。

sentences.en: because they don't have the sufficient mental resources to deal with this added stress.
sentences.zh: 因为他们没有足够的心理资源来应对这种额外的压力。

sentences.en: Remember, in those moments though, all this alarm system is trying to do is help you, not harm you.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，在那些时刻，这个警报系统所做的一切都是为了帮助你，而不是伤害你。

sentences.en: It's just your job in that moment to consciously interpret whether the system is getting it wrong and correct that perception.
sentences.zh: 你当时的工作只是有意识地去解读这个系统是否出错了，并纠正那种认知。

sentences.en: The important thing I want to remind you is that panic attacks just cannot last forever, it is not physically possible.
sentences.zh: 我想提醒你重要的一点是，恐慌发作是不可能永远持续下去的，这在生理上是不可能的。

sentences.en: we will reach a point of exhaustion, right?
sentences.zh: 我们总会达到精疲力竭的地步，对吧？

sentences.en: It's taking so much out of you.
sentences.zh: 它会消耗你太多的精力。

sentences.en: Most therapists or psychologists will tell you that a panic attack is probably going to peak around 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 大多数治疗师或心理学家会告诉你，恐慌发作通常会在10分钟左右达到顶峰。

sentences.en: It will most likely, most certainly subside within an hour, within half an hour most of the time.
sentences.zh: 它极有可能，甚至肯定会在一小时内，大多数情况下在半小时内消退。

sentences.en: Sometimes obviously we can have multiple panic attacks in a row, so there'll be a small period where you're not panicking.
sentences.zh: 显然，有时我们会连续多次恐慌发作，所以中间会有一小段不恐慌的时间。

sentences.en: Sometimes we can misinterpret that and feel like we've had a panic attack for like a whole day, but people will tell you this is not one long continuous panic attacks, but one
sentences.zh: 有时我们可能会误解这一点，感觉自己好像整整一天都在恐慌，但人们会告诉你，这并不是一次漫长的持续性恐慌发作，而是

sentences.en: long, sorry, continuous panic attack, but multiple smaller panic attacks.
sentences.zh: 漫长的，抱歉，持续性的恐慌发作，而是多次较小的恐慌发作。

sentences.en: Panic just takes so much out of you though.
sentences.zh: 不过，恐慌确实会消耗你太多的精力。

sentences.en: We genuinely do not have the resources to sustain such a feeling.
sentences.zh: 我们确实没有资源来维持这种感觉。

sentences.en: this system that alarms you and sets you off and creates all of these changes in your body.
sentences.zh: 这个让你警觉、触发你并导致你身体发生所有这些变化的系统。

sentences.en: It is meant for small, concentrated bursts of energy.
sentences.zh: 它是为了短促、集中的能量爆发而设计的。

sentences.en: So over time, all that, it takes so much of your energy that you're going to run out.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，所有这些都会消耗你太多的能量，以至于你会耗尽。

sentences.en: And I actually think that that's really nice to know.
sentences.zh: 而且我实际上认为知道这一点真的很好。

sentences.en: You will get through this.
sentences.zh: 你会挺过去的。

sentences.en: You have to reach an exhaustion point or a breaking point.
sentences.zh: 你必须达到精疲力竭或崩溃的临界点。

sentences.en: Now the reason you might be experiencing a greater number of repetitive panic attacks, it might have to do with something in your environment or within your internal state that
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能经历更多重复性恐慌发作的原因，可能与你环境或内部状态中的某些因素有关，

sentences.en: is causing you to feel unsafe.
sentences.zh: 导致你感到不安全。

sentences.en: It doesn't necessarily need to be some big, crazy, eccentric,
sentences.zh: 它不一定非得是什么巨大的、疯狂的、古怪的，

sentences.en: you know, very obvious threat in your environment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，环境中非常明显的威胁。

sentences.en: For example, there was a time maybe two or three years ago where my panic attacks were terrible.
sentences.zh: 例如，大约两三年前，我曾有一段时间恐慌发作得非常厉害。

sentences.en: They were awful.
sentences.zh: 那真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: They were so, so frustrating.
sentences.zh: 它们让人非常、非常沮丧。

sentences.en: They happened all the time without control.
sentences.zh: 它们总是毫无控制地发生。

sentences.en: And also without seemingly a trigger, you know, I would be in bed and I would be panicking.
sentences.zh: 而且似乎也没有触发因素，你知道，我躺在床上也会恐慌。

sentences.en: What I began to realize was that actually the last few months when I looked back at them had been really, really rough, really, really hard.
sentences.zh: 我开始意识到，实际上当我回顾过去几个月时，那段时间真的非常、非常艰难，非常、非常辛苦。

sentences.en: I don't know if I want to go into it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否想深入谈论它。

sentences.en: And this was in the past, so maybe I will give you some detail.
sentences.zh: 但这已经是过去的事了，所以也许我会给你一些细节。

sentences.en: Like there had been a lot of conflict going on in my life with friends.
sentences.zh: 比如我的生活中与朋友之间发生了很多冲突。

sentences.en: I was moving to a new city.
sentences.zh: 我正要搬到一个新的城市。

sentences.en: I was graduating from university.
sentences.zh: 我正要从大学毕业。

sentences.en: I was saying goodbye to people.
sentences.zh: 我正在和人们告别。

sentences.en: I was going through a breakup.
sentences.zh: 我正在经历一场分手。

sentences.en: There was, I was just slowly being worn down.
sentences.zh: 我只是在慢慢地被磨损。

sentences.en: I was taking a lot of my friends' problems on as well.
sentences.zh: 我也承担了很多朋友的问题。

sentences.en: And I realized when I started, actually at the tail end of this period of panic that this had been coming up for a while.
sentences.zh: 当我开始意识到时，实际上是在这段恐慌期的末尾，这种情况已经持续了一段时间了。

sentences.en: Like this was, had been in the works.
sentences.zh: 就像这是，一直在酝酿之中。

sentences.en: This had been slowly brewing.
sentences.zh: 这一直在慢慢发酵。

sentences.en: But I kept suppressing it because I just was like, I don't have time to deal with this right now.
sentences.zh: 但我一直压抑着它，因为我当时想，我现在没时间处理这个。

sentences.en: I don't have time for a panic attack.
sentences.zh: 我没时间恐慌发作。

sentences.en: I don't have time.
sentences.zh: 我没时间。

sentences.en: And the longer I held back that wave, the stronger it eventually was when it burst through.
sentences.zh: 我压制那股浪潮的时间越长，它最终爆发时就越强烈。

sentences.en: The thing though about panic and fear is that although they definitely are villainized because they are uncomfortable, sometimes you actually just have to feel it to
sentences.zh: 然而，关于恐慌和恐惧的一点是，虽然它们因为让人不适而肯定被妖魔化了，但有时你实际上必须去感受它，才能

sentences.en: get through it.
sentences.zh: 挺过去。

sentences.en: Putting it off is going to make it worse in the long run.
sentences.zh: 推迟它只会让情况在长期内变得更糟。

sentences.en: It's almost like playing whack-a-mole, right?
sentences.zh: 这就像在玩打地鼠游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: Like every time you see like the nose of the panic attack popping out, you try and hit it down and hit it down.
sentences.zh: 就像每次你看到恐慌发作的苗头冒出来，你就试图把它打下去，再打下去。

sentences.en: But if you just let them pop up, they'll eventually go away and you'll exert less energy trying to control everything in your environment to ensure that you don't feel fear
sentences.zh: 但如果你只是让它们冒出来，它们最终会消失，而你为了确保自己不感到恐惧，试图控制环境中一切所消耗的能量会更少，

sentences.en: when fear is actually a really natural response.
sentences.zh: 而恐惧实际上是一种非常自然的反应。

sentences.en: Anxiety and panic actually serves a purpose.
sentences.zh: 焦虑和恐慌实际上是有目的的。

sentences.en: It might indicate that something is wrong and that you're unable to
sentences.zh: 它可能表明出了问题，你无法

sentences.en: reach a state or a balance of homeostasis.
sentences.zh: 达到一种稳态或平衡。

sentences.en: It might show you that there is an ongoing stressor that you need to deal with.
sentences.zh: 它可能向你展示有一个你需要处理的持续压力源。

sentences.en: And when we see people who don't have that fear response at all, I always think about Alex
sentences.zh: 当我们看到那些根本没有恐惧反应的人时，我总是想到亚历克斯·霍诺德（Alex Honnold），

sentences.en: Honnold, the very famous free-selling rock climber.
sentences.zh: 那位非常有名的徒手攀岩者。

sentences.en: He's one of them.
sentences.zh: 他是其中之一。

sentences.en: These individuals obviously have like a smaller amygdala, a smaller fear center of the brain.
sentences.zh: 这些人显然有一个较小的杏仁核，即大脑中较小的恐惧中心。

sentences.en: And they can't always identify danger.
sentences.zh: 他们并不总能识别危险。

sentences.en: They often do risky things.
sentences.zh: 他们经常做冒险的事情。

sentences.en: They can't always as well identify other people's emotions.
sentences.zh: 他们也不总能识别他人的情绪。

sentences.en: It's often the people who are most anxious that are also the most empathetic.
sentences.zh: 通常最焦虑的人也是最有同理心的人。

sentences.en: And in some ways, maybe this is a very big claim, but also the most intelligent because they are the ones who are sitting there thinking everything through, thinking
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这可能是一个很大的主张，但他们也是最聪明的，因为他们是那些坐在那里把一切都想透的人，思考

sentences.en: how everyone else is feeling, thinking how everything can go wrong, all of that catastrophizing.
sentences.zh: 别人感觉如何，思考一切可能出错的地方，所有这些灾难化思维。

sentences.en: That's a lot of big brain exercises right there.
sentences.zh: 那可是非常大的大脑练习。

sentences.en: Regardless, though, of how quote-unquote functional panic and anxiety might be to us as humans from a scientific point of view, I'm sure that if you are someone who
sentences.zh: 然而，无论从科学角度来看，恐慌和焦虑对我们人类来说有多么所谓的“功能性”，我相信如果你是一个

sentences.en: has panic attacks, you have had a few moments where you would have given anything to live a life without them.
sentences.zh: 会恐慌发作的人，你一定有过几次时刻，愿意付出一切来过一种没有它们的生活。

sentences.en: They're scary.
sentences.zh: 它们很可怕。

sentences.en: They're so debilitating.
sentences.zh: 它们非常令人衰弱。

sentences.en: They're inconvenient.
sentences.zh: 它们很不方便。

sentences.en: We don't like feeling disrupted by an emotion that we can't control.
sentences.zh: 我们不喜欢被一种我们无法控制的情绪所干扰。

sentences.en: And I get that.
sentences.zh: 我明白这一点。

sentences.en: I really, really get that.
sentences.zh: 我真的、真的明白这一点。

sentences.en: Now, not everything is going to be entirely effective for you in managing this.
sentences.zh: 当然，并不是所有方法对你管理焦虑都完全有效。

sentences.en: Don't keep forcing habits or practices on yourself that don't work because you're just going to feel more frustrated and less in control because you're trying and not succeeding.
sentences.zh: 不要强迫自己去执行那些没用的习惯或练习，因为那样只会让你感到更沮丧、更失控，因为你在尝试却没成功。

sentences.en: I have a checklist in my phone of everything that I know works for me.
sentences.zh: 我的手机里有一个清单，记录着所有我知道对我有效的方法。

sentences.en: And there are about, I think at this stage, over 30 things that I know I can do that are going to calm me down.
sentences.zh: 我想现阶段大概有30多种我知道可以让我平静下来的方法。

sentences.en: So if the first one doesn't work or the second one probably will.
sentences.zh: 所以如果第一个没用，第二个很可能会有用。

sentences.en: And if that one doesn't work, I've got the third, fifth, all the way to
sentences.zh: 如果那个也没用，我还有第三个、第五个，一直到

sentences.en: 30 of options for me.
sentences.zh: 第30个选择。

sentences.en: And even the understanding and even like the fact that I know I have that list makes me feel so much better because I know that I have resources and options available that I'm not
sentences.zh: 甚至仅仅是理解这一点，仅仅是知道我有那个清单，就让我感觉好多了，因为我知道我有可用的资源和选择，我不会

sentences.en: going to be stuck in that panicked moment because I've done that before.
sentences.zh: 被困在那个恐慌的时刻，因为我以前经历过。

sentences.en: The biggest ones for me are meditations.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，最有效的是冥想。

sentences.en: I love going through my photo albums as a distraction, cleaning out all my photos.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢翻看我的相册作为消遣，清理所有的照片。

sentences.en: And I have my affirmations, my little reminders that I have survived this before.
sentences.zh: 我还有我的肯定语，那些提醒我以前曾挺过来的小纸条。

sentences.en: I will survive this now.
sentences.zh: 我现在也能挺过去。

sentences.en: I am safe.
sentences.zh: 我是安全的。

sentences.en: I'm going to inhale the good thoughts, exhale the bad ones.
sentences.zh: 我要吸入好的想法，呼出坏的想法。

sentences.en: And I'm just going to sit with that feeling for a little bit and give it give it a chance to hurt me.
sentences.zh: 我就坐在那里，感受这种感觉一会儿，给它一个伤害我的机会。

sentences.en: And after a while, I realize that it won't.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，我意识到它不会。

sentences.en: It won't hurt me.
sentences.zh: 它伤害不了我。

sentences.en: The final thing that really helps me that I return to again and again in my own life are these short five minute visualization exercises that I can put on, listen to, and I find it
sentences.zh: 最后一件对我真正有帮助，且我在生活中反复使用的，是这些简短的五分钟可视化练习，我可以播放、聆听，我发现它

sentences.en: really calms me down.
sentences.zh: 真的能让我平静下来。

sentences.en: I even imagine them when I don't have immediate access to that audio, like on a plane or someone without Wi-Fi or an internet.
sentences.zh: 即使在没有音频的情况下，比如在飞机上，或者没有Wi-Fi或网络的地方，我也会想象这些练习。

sentences.en: So I want you to pause with me for a second.
sentences.zh: 所以我想让你和我一起暂停一下。

sentences.en: And we're going to go through one together right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在就一起做一个练习。

sentences.en: I know that right now it feels like your panic is taking over.
sentences.zh: 我知道现在你感觉恐慌正在占据上风。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: Remember, it is just a feeling.
sentences.zh: 记住，这只是一种感觉。

sentences.en: No different to feeling joyful or frustrated or happy or angry.
sentences.zh: 和感到快乐、沮丧、高兴或愤怒没什么不同。

sentences.en: These emotions exist only within you.
sentences.zh: 这些情绪只存在于你的内心。

sentences.en: And your panic is not going to hurt you.
sentences.zh: 你的恐慌伤害不了你。

sentences.en: It is not physical.
sentences.zh: 它不是物理性的。

sentences.en: It has come from you and therefore you can control it.
sentences.zh: 它源于你，因此你可以控制它。

sentences.en: I'm here with you now in this moment and you and I are like partners.
sentences.zh: 我现在和你在一起，你和我就像伙伴一样。

sentences.en: I'm going to watch out for you whilst you take some time to realign all of your senses, make sense of this feeling.
sentences.zh: 我会守护着你，同时你花点时间重新调整你的感官，理清这种感觉。

sentences.en: And in only a few minutes, you're going to be able to return to whatever it is you were just doing.
sentences.zh: 只需几分钟，你就能回到你刚才正在做的事情上。

sentences.en: Don't worry about what's going on around you.
sentences.zh: 别担心周围发生了什么。

sentences.en: I can do that for you.
sentences.zh: 我可以帮你处理。

sentences.en: All I need you to focus on right now is your body and what you're feeling.
sentences.zh: 现在我只需要你专注于你的身体和你正在感受的东西。

sentences.en: I want you to focus on your breathing with me.
sentences.zh: 我想让你和我一起专注于呼吸。

sentences.en: We're going to breathe in for five seconds now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在吸气五秒钟。

sentences.en: Five.
sentences.zh: 五。

sentences.en: Four.
sentences.zh: 四。

sentences.en: Three.
sentences.zh: 三。

sentences.en: Two.
sentences.zh: 二。

sentences.en: One.
sentences.zh: 一。

sentences.en: Now hold for five.
sentences.zh: 现在憋气五秒。

sentences.en: Four.
sentences.zh: 四。

sentences.en: Three.
sentences.zh: 三。

sentences.en: Three.
sentences.zh: 三。

sentences.en: Two.
sentences.zh: 二。

sentences.en: One.
sentences.zh: 一。

sentences.en: And breathe out for five seconds.
sentences.zh: 呼气五秒钟。

sentences.en: Good job.
sentences.zh: 做得好。

sentences.en: I knew that wouldn't be too hard.
sentences.zh: 我就知道这不会太难。

sentences.en: I want you to pause for a second and repeat that three more times.
sentences.zh: 我想让你暂停一下，再重复三次。

sentences.en: I'm sure you're feeling better now.
sentences.zh: 我相信你现在感觉好多了。

sentences.en: I can see that.
sentences.zh: 我看得出来。

sentences.en: Good job.
sentences.zh: 做得好。

sentences.en: I'm proud of you.
sentences.zh: 我为你感到骄傲。

sentences.en: Now I want you to focus on your heartbeat for a few seconds.
sentences.zh: 现在我想让你专注于心跳几秒钟。

sentences.en: As you take a few more deep breaths, just notice how it begins to slow down.
sentences.zh: 当你再做几次深呼吸时，注意它如何开始慢下来。

sentences.en: You're doing that because you're in control.
sentences.zh: 你做到了，因为你在掌控之中。

sentences.en: Your anxiety doesn't have as much control as it would like.
sentences.zh: 你的焦虑并没有它想要的那么大的控制权。

sentences.en: You are the one in charge.
sentences.zh: 你才是掌控者。

sentences.en: You're a bit like a scientist in this moment.
sentences.zh: 这一刻你就像个科学家。

sentences.en: I want you to think of this panic you're feeling as an interesting specimen you want to understand better.
sentences.zh: 我想让你把这种恐慌感看作是一个你想深入了解的有趣样本。

sentences.en: It's sitting right in front of you behind a nice reinforced pane of glass.
sentences.zh: 它正坐在你面前，隔着一块漂亮的强化玻璃。

sentences.en: It can't hurt you.
sentences.zh: 它伤害不了你。

sentences.en: It can't touch you.
sentences.zh: 它碰不到你。

sentences.en: But you can observe it and notice what it's responding to.
sentences.zh: 但你可以观察它，注意它对什么有反应。

sentences.en: As you relax, it will too.
sentences.zh: 当你放松时，它也会放松。

sentences.en: And if you can't, that is okay.
sentences.zh: 如果做不到，也没关系。

sentences.en: You can always walk out of the room and leave your anxiety behind.
sentences.zh: 你随时可以走出房间，把焦虑留在身后。

sentences.en: It is not going to escape.
sentences.zh: 它逃不掉的。

sentences.en: It's not going to hurt you because you are in control.
sentences.zh: 它伤害不了你，因为你在掌控之中。

sentences.en: You have the key and you alone.
sentences.zh: 钥匙在你手里，只有你才有。

sentences.en: To test this, I want you to give your anxiety
sentences.zh: 为了测试这一点，我想让你给你的焦虑

sentences.en: 30 seconds to break free.
sentences.zh: 30秒的时间去挣脱。

sentences.en: 30 seconds to try and escape, to take over, to do its worSt.
sentences.zh: 30秒的时间去尝试逃跑、去占据上风、去尽情作恶。

sentences.en: You're being really generous with your anxiety.
sentences.zh: 你对你的焦虑真的很慷慨。

sentences.en: You don't have to do this for it.
sentences.zh: 你没必要为它这样做。

sentences.en: But you are deciding to be kind today.
sentences.zh: 但你今天决定要善良一点。

sentences.en: You're going to look at your anxiety right now and say, okay, it's your turn.
sentences.zh: 你现在要看着你的焦虑说：好吧，轮到你了。

sentences.en: Do whatever you would like.
sentences.zh: 做你想做的任何事吧。

sentences.en: Destroy the room.
sentences.zh: 毁掉这个房间。

sentences.en: Jump around.
sentences.zh: 跳来跳去。

sentences.en: Whatever you want to do.
sentences.zh: 随你喜欢。

sentences.en: But after 30 seconds, you have had your chance and now it's my turn.
sentences.zh: 但30秒后，你的机会用完了，现在轮到我了。

sentences.en: So let's count down together.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一起倒数。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: You might feel like your anxiety is fighting very hard right now to get out of that room.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得你的焦虑现在正拼命想逃出那个房间。

sentences.en: But it's still trapped behind that glass while you're sitting calmly in that nice, comfortable chair watching each of its moves, not needing to react.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然被困在玻璃后面，而你正平静地坐在那把舒适的椅子上，看着它的一举一动，无需做出反应。

sentences.en: Your anxiety is getting tired now.
sentences.zh: 你的焦虑现在已经感到疲惫了。

sentences.en: You can see it losing its steam.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它正在失去动力。

sentences.en: It knows it's not going to win.
sentences.zh: 它知道自己赢不了。

sentences.en: This time or the next.
sentences.zh: 无论是这次还是下次。

sentences.en: It's slowly losing its energy.
sentences.zh: 它正在慢慢失去能量。

sentences.en: Your anxiety has run out of energy.
sentences.zh: 你的焦虑已经耗尽了能量。

sentences.en: It's not screaming or yelling anymore.
sentences.zh: 它不再尖叫或咆哮了。

sentences.en: It is slowing down.
sentences.zh: 它正在慢下来。

sentences.en: Its eyes are closing.
sentences.zh: 它的眼睛正在闭上。

sentences.en: there's your anxiety, sitting calmly in the corner.
sentences.zh: 看，你的焦虑正平静地坐在角落里。

sentences.en: Now, it's your time.
sentences.zh: 现在，轮到你了。

sentences.en: Focus on your breath again for me.
sentences.zh: 再为我专注于你的呼吸。

sentences.en: Breathe in again for 5,
sentences.zh: 再次吸气，数5下，

sentences.en: Now we're going to hold.
sentences.zh: 现在我们要屏住呼吸。

sentences.en: And finally, breathe out with me.
sentences.zh: 最后，跟我一起呼气。

sentences.en: If you need to, you can do that a few more times.
sentences.zh: 如果需要，你可以多做几次。

sentences.en: It's always going to be up to you.
sentences.zh: 这始终取决于你自己。

sentences.en: As you continue to breathe deeply,
sentences.zh: 当你继续深呼吸时，

sentences.en: I want to remind you that you are safe and supported in this moment.
sentences.zh: 我想提醒你，此时此刻你是安全的，并得到支持。

sentences.en: Panic attacks can be overwhelming, but you have the strength within you to overcome them, like you just did.
sentences.zh: 恐慌发作可能会让人不知所措，但你内心拥有克服它们的力量，就像你刚才做到的那样。

sentences.en: Remember to be gentle with yourself and to acknowledge those feelings.
sentences.zh: 记得要善待自己，并接纳那些感受。

sentences.en: You are so capable and brave and strong and I am so proud of you.
sentences.zh: 你非常有能力、勇敢且坚强，我为你感到骄傲。

sentences.en: I want you to talk to your panic now.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想让你和你的恐慌对话。

sentences.en: Talk to your anxiety.
sentences.zh: 和你的焦虑对话。

sentences.en: You can see, really, that it's just this weak little creature sitting in the corner of the room.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，它其实只是一个坐在房间角落里虚弱的小生物。

sentences.en: You feel slightly sorry for it and you're going to speak to it with compassion.
sentences.zh: 你对它感到一丝怜悯，并准备带着同情心与它交谈。

sentences.en: I know you're scared, anxiety, and that's okay.
sentences.zh: 我知道你很害怕，焦虑，没关系的。

sentences.en: I'm going to be gentle with you.
sentences.zh: 我会温柔地对待你。

sentences.en: You can be at peace here.
sentences.zh: 你可以在这里感到平静。

sentences.en: Nothing is wrong.
sentences.zh: 一切都很好。

sentences.en: We are alive.
sentences.zh: 我们还活着。

sentences.en: We are breathing.
sentences.zh: 我们正在呼吸。

sentences.en: We are loved.
sentences.zh: 我们被爱着。

sentences.en: And you are welcome here.
sentences.zh: 这里欢迎你。

sentences.en: I know that you have been misunderstood in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我知道你过去一直被误解。

sentences.en: I know I've been scared of you.
sentences.zh: 我知道我曾经害怕过你。

sentences.en: But I can see that under that scary exterior, you are just an emotion trying to be seen.
sentences.zh: 但我能看出，在那可怕的外表下，你只是一个渴望被看见的情绪。

sentences.en: I see you.
sentences.zh: 我看见你了。

sentences.en: I acknowledge you.
sentences.zh: 我接纳你。

sentences.en: You can stay here for a while, but in exchange, you don't get to be in control.
sentences.zh: 你可以待在这里一会儿，但作为交换，你不能掌控一切。

sentences.en: I'm in control.
sentences.zh: 由我来掌控。

sentences.en: So feel free to get comfy, to reSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，请随意放松，休息一下。

sentences.en: Let me know if you need anything.
sentences.zh: 如果需要什么，随时告诉我。

sentences.en: We can talk again.
sentences.zh: 我们可以再聊。

sentences.en: But for now,
sentences.zh: 但现在，

sentences.en: I'm going to leave this room and get on with my day.
sentences.zh: 我要离开这个房间，继续我的一天了。

sentences.en: I'm going to leave in three,
sentences.zh: 我要在三声后离开，

sentences.en: two,
sentences.zh: 二，

sentences.en: one.
sentences.zh: 一。

sentences.en: Goodbye, anxiety.
sentences.zh: 再见，焦虑。

sentences.en: Are you feeling better?
sentences.zh: 你感觉好点了吗？

sentences.en: I really hope so.
sentences.zh: 我真心希望如此。

sentences.en: And if not, please feel free to listen again.
sentences.zh: 如果还没有，请随时再听一遍。

sentences.en: When we visualize our anxiety as something that is harmless, something that we can see, we can hold, that we can approach, we release a lot of that additional fear
sentences.zh: 当我们把焦虑想象成某种无害的东西，某种我们可以看见、可以掌控、可以接近的东西时，我们就释放了许多围绕着它能对我们做什么、能造成什么伤害的额外恐惧。

sentences.en: we have around what it can do to us, the harm it can cause.
sentences.zh: 我们所拥有的关于它能对我们做什么，以及它可能造成的伤害的恐惧。

sentences.en: Because at the end of the day, something that we forget is that it is just another emotion and you are the house, the home of all of these emotions.
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，我们容易忘记的一点是，它只是另一种情绪，而你是所有这些情绪的居所，是它们的家。

sentences.en: They are you.
sentences.zh: 它们就是你的一部分。

sentences.en: You have the final say.
sentences.zh: 你拥有最终决定权。

sentences.en: I really hope that this episode helped you, just giving you more information about what panic attacks actually are, guiding you through what to do about it, some of my tactics
sentences.zh: 我真心希望这一集能对你有所帮助，为你提供更多关于恐慌发作本质的信息，引导你如何应对，并分享我的一些策略

sentences.en: and my tips, providing you with that psychoeducation.
sentences.zh: 和建议，为你提供心理健康教育。

sentences.en: I hope you're just feeling better.
sentences.zh: 希望你现在感觉好多了。

sentences.en: I hope that if you need to return to this episode that you do, it will always be here.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要重温这一集，请随时回来，它会一直在这里。

sentences.en: Feel free to come back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎随时回来。

sentences.en: I will still be here eternally in this little voice, in this little episode clip.
sentences.zh: 我会永远留在这个小小的声音里，留在这个小小的剧集片段里。

sentences.en: But if there is someone you know who might need to hear this, please feel free to share it with them.
sentences.zh: 但如果你认识的人可能需要听到这些，请随时分享给他们。

sentences.en: As always, if you enjoyed this episode, please feel free to leave a five-star review wherever you are listening right now.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，如果你喜欢这一集，请在你收听的平台上留下五星好评。

sentences.en: If you liked this episode, I know it's a bit different to what I usually do.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这一集，我知道这和我平时的风格有点不同。

sentences.en: Please let me know if it was of any help, if you would like me to do more episodes like this.
sentences.zh: 如果它对你有任何帮助，或者你希望我多做一些这样的节目，请告诉我。

sentences.en: You can DM me over on Instagram at thatpsychologypodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Instagram 上私信我，账号是 thatpsychologypodcast。

sentences.en: I would love to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 我很期待收到你的消息。

sentences.en: I'm sending you love.
sentences.zh: 我为你送上爱。

sentences.en: I'm sending you strength.
sentences.zh: 我为你送上力量。

sentences.en: I'm proud of you.
sentences.zh: 我为你感到骄傲。

sentences.en: Good job.
sentences.zh: 做得好。

sentences.en: You got through it.
sentences.zh: 你挺过来了。

sentences.en: And we will be back next week with another episode.
sentences.zh: 下周我们会带着另一集回来。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 今年我对待健康的方式有了很大的改变。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去总是专注于最大化产出和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 但现在我意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my whoop.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我沉迷于我的 Whoop。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information driven person and I love opening my whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood,
sentences.zh: 说真的，你们知道我是一个非常注重数据和信息的人，我喜欢打开 Whoop 应用程序，看看我的睡眠、压力和身体负荷如何与我的情绪相关联，

sentences.en: with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day to day.
sentences.zh: 以及与我的跑步表现和日常感受的关联。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit and I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么精英运动员，但我确实从中受益匪浅，而且我也真的很享受了解更多关于自己身体的信息。

sentences.en: And whoop also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day to day about what I need
sentences.zh: Whoop 还为我提供了这些可操作的、个性化的见解，让我变得更加有意识，意味着我每天都能针对自己的需求做出更明智的决定，

sentences.en: rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 而不是一味地踩油门，不停地奔波。

sentences.en: New members can try whoop with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新用户可以在订阅会员前，先通过 30 天免费试用体验 Whoop。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of whoop.
